question: A woman comes to the OPD 6 weeks after copper IUCD insertion reporting that she cannot feel the threads during self-examination. On speculum examination, no threads are visible at the external os. What is the MOST appropriate next step in management?

answers.text: Advise the patient that thread retraction is normal and no further action is needed

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Missing threads always require investigation. Possible explanations include threads retracted into the cavity (usually benign), IUD expulsion, uterine perforation, or pregnancy — each requires a different management.

answers.text: Perform pelvic ultrasound to confirm IUCD position within the uterine cavity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Pelvic ultrasound is the first investigation. It confirms whether the IUCD is in situ within the uterine cavity (threads retracted), expelled (not visible on USS), or has perforated (not in cavity — plain X-ray needed to locate).

answers.text: Immediately attempt to remove the IUCD with ring forceps under direct vision at the os

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Blind forceps attempts without imaging risk uterine trauma and are inappropriate when threads are not visible. Ultrasound must confirm device position first.

answers.text: Repeat speculum examination next cycle when the cervix is softer and threads may reappear

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Deferring investigation is unsafe. Threads do not reliably reappear on their own, and a perforated or expelled IUCD provides no contraceptive protection. Immediate ultrasound is required.

overallFeedback.feedback: When IUCD threads are missing, pelvic ultrasound is the first step. This determines whether the device is correctly in situ (threads retracted into cavity), expelled, or has perforated the uterus.
Correct. Pelvic ultrasound is the first step when IUCD threads are missing — it distinguishes in-situ thread retraction (common, benign) from expulsion or perforation (both requiring further action).
